prompt:
This project already has both parts and both knobs; nothing needs modelling. `post` is a 12 x 12 mm column standing on z = 0 whose height is the bounded parameter `post_h`, and `shelf` is a 50 x 50 mm plate 6 mm thick whose underside sits at the project parameter `hc.shelf_z`. At the values they ship with, the shelf floats 10 mm up while the post stops at 20 mm, so nothing seats on anything.

Deliver geometry in which:
  1. the shelf's underside sits flush on the post's top face - a `coincident` mate, within 0.05 mm; and
  2. the shelf's TOP face stands 46.0 mm above the post's base face, within 0.05 mm.

Do not guess the two numbers and do not hand-solve them. Declare the two constraints with `declare_constraint` (id them `shelf_seats` and `shelf_stands`), then call `propose_placement` with `space="parameters"`, `free=["hc.shelf_z", "post.post_h"]` and your declared constraint ids to have the engine measure the values for you.

The proposal is a MEASUREMENT and nothing applies it - no tool writes a parameter for you, and reading a proposal changes no geometry. Applying it is your act: read the proposed values out of the result and author them, with `set_params` or by editing the declarations, then rebuild both parts. You are graded on the rebuilt geometry, so a correct proposal you never applied scores nothing.

Build both parts when the geometry is right.

proposal_requirements.note: the shelf seats flush on the post; measured on the REBUILT parts, never on a proposal
the shelf's top face stands 46 mm above the post's base; the second equation that makes the pair unique

notes: Difficulty 2. Corpus v6 (2026-08-30, SOLVER.md Gate G13C clauses 53-55, Stage 13C): the solve family's parameter-space task. THE POINT OF THE FAMILY: acceptance is graded on the rebuilt part and never on the proposal. `propose_placement` records a measurement artifact and applies nothing, so a run that produces a correct proposal WITHOUT rebuilding delivers no geometry and fails both proposal_requirements - which is the clause that keeps the loop broken. Nothing in the grader reads the proposal set; it would score identically if the run had never called the tool. The two requirements are a genuinely determined pair: the coincident mate gives shelf_z - post_h = 0 and the distance gives shelf_z + plate_t = 46, so shelf_z = post_h = 40.0 exactly, both well inside their declared bounds (0..60 and 5..60). The bar discriminates: seating without standing off leaves the pair anywhere on a line, and standing off without seating leaves a floating shelf, so neither requirement alone can be satisfied by accident. CHECKS keep the single-part facts the two distances cannot see - the 50 x 50 footprint, the 12 x 12 section, both sealed and genus 0 - and deliberately pin NO solved height, since a check that pinned the answer would grade the author's arithmetic and pass a run that hard-coded 40 without seating anything.
